name: Ballantine Gymnasium
description: An early campus gymnasium on the site of the old College Field; fire destroyed most of it in January 1930, and the College Avenue Gymnasium replaced it.
notes: Fire destroyed most of it Jan 7 1930 (Rutgers timeline cited by Wikipedia; NYT Jan 8 1930 quoted on a Rivals thread; two sources). Rear reportedly survived the fire; a garbled web page says parts of the facade remain near George Street, unverified. Year built BLANK: a gym was built on the College Field site in 1892, but no source found says Ballantine was that building (Rutgers archive entries mention Ballantine 1907-1916). Needs archive check. | LOCATION LEAD NOT CONFIRMED (coordinates left blank): the lead that Ballantine stood on the College Avenue Gymnasium site is contradicted by Wikipedia's Voorhees Mall article, which says the Zimmerli Art Museum expanded over the remains of the Ballantine Gym and that the College Avenue Gymnasium was built a few blocks away. The Wikipedia College Avenue Gymnasium article says the Barn replaced an earlier gym on the old College Field site (1892), which may be a different building. One unverified web page also says parts of the Ballantine facade remain near the Zimmerli/George Street parking lot. Needs a Sanborn map or Rutgers Special Collections to pin the site.
